name: Orthosiphon (java tea)
short: Healthy people: authors call urine oxalate excretion on Orthosiphon tea unfavourable, possibly raising stone risk. Lab: inhibited human UGT enzymes (possible drug interactions). Rodents: no toxicity.
text: In a study in healthy people (the abstract gives no numbers), drinking Orthosiphon tea made the urine more alkaline, but the authors describe the excretion of oxalate in the urine as an unfavourable effect that may result in a higher risk of stone formation; they add that all parameters were within normal limits and that the study may or may not apply to people with stones. The abstracts of two trials in stone formers, a 14-day placebo-controlled trial of Orthosiphon extract capsules in 76 people and a trial of up to 18 months comparing Orthosiphon grandiflorus tea with the medicine sodium potassium citrate in 48 people, do not mention any adverse events with Orthosiphon (the second reports fatigue and loss of appetite in 26.3% of the citrate group); this does not show that none occurred. The remaining evidence comes from animal and laboratory studies of Orthosiphon stamineus extracts (leaf extracts in the two rat studies; the genotoxicity and enzyme studies do not name the plant part). In rats, single doses of 5000 mg/kg of aqueous, 50% aqueous-ethanol and ethanol leaf extracts by mouth caused no toxic effects or deaths over 14 days, and a 50% methanol leaf extract given by gavage at up to 5000 mg/kg a day for 28 days caused no deaths, no signs of toxicity and no differences in blood tests or organs. An aqueous extract did not cause mutations in bacterial tests and did not increase micronuclei in mouse bone marrow when given by gavage. In a laboratory study with recombinant human UGT (glucuronidation) enzymes, an Orthosiphon stamineus extract inhibited most of the isoforms tested in a concentration-dependent way, and the authors suggest a potential for drug-herbal extract interactions; the cited sources do not test whether this happens in people, and no specific medicines are named.
